acceptance: Partitioning balances by recorded per-test duration
Worst-shard time within about 15% of the mean across at least 10 PR runs
Medium critical path shorter than the pre-shrink unit chain
Shard coverage evidence still verifies every collected test
context: From the CI timing analysis in this session. Related open item ci-amplab-generate-data-timeout-flake covers the generate_data timeout flake itself.
description: After the fast tier shrank, shard 3 of medium-test received most of the moved tests. The last timing analysis (runs to 2026-10-18 17:02Z) shows shard 3 at about 841 s against 496-630 s for the others; the critical path ci-paths -> medium-collect -> medium-test (shard 3) -> core is 17.0 min against 16.5 min before, so end-to-end CI on PRs that run medium shards is about 3% slower. An even split would be about 620 s per shard, a chain of roughly 800 s. A later run showed shard 0 at 16m53s with tests/test_h2odb.py::TestH2ODB::test_generate_data alone taking 353 s, so partitioning should weight by recorded duration rather than count.
